study: NeoDevEx token benchmark (case-studies/tokens/bench/run_bench.py), self-hosted model re-run

setup.model: openai/qwen3-coder-next (RedHatAI/Qwen3-Coder-Next-NVFP4 on vLLM 0.30.0, 1x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, Runpod)
setup.agent_settings: out/neo-agent-settings.json + out/neo-automation-tail.txt (the 'neo' variant of round 3, the latest round in out/results.jsonl). It is identical to the current app dump (out/app-agent-settings.json) except that the app dump carries the newer chat-study AGENT_WORKING_RULES text in system_message_suffix; neo was kept so the comparison with the Gemini rows uses byte-identical settings.
setup.runner: scratchpad wrapper that imports run_bench.py unchanged and patches only the LLM config (base_url, api_key, caching_prompt=False, no reasoning params, timeout 600). Same tasks, fixture, MAX_ITERATIONS=60, success checks.
setup.concurrency: 3 runner processes in parallel (one per rep), each running T1..T5 sequentially. For the first ~3 minutes the pod was also serving 3 qwen chat-bench processes from another session.
setup.comparison: Gemini 2.5 Flash rows from out/results.jsonl (round 3, 4 reps each): 'neo' = same settings as qwen; 'lean' = best Gemini variant overall (17/20, lowest median tokens); 'today' = pre-change baseline.
setup.success_judging: run_bench.py TASKS[*].check, unchanged (same as existing results).

headline.qwen_pass_rate: 15/15 by the harness check (14/15 on manual audit, see findings)

money.price_source: PRICES table in case-studies/chat/bench/summarize.py (USD per 1M tokens input/output/cached-input): gemini-4-argon 2.00/10.00/0.10 (the frontier model and the app default), gemini-2.5-flash 0.30/2.50/0.03. Formula identical to that file's cost(): (input-cached)*in + cached*cached + output*out.
money.note: qwen runs report 0 cached tokens (vLLM returns no cache usage and caching_prompt was off), so 'at_*_prices_usd_total' charges every qwen input token at the full rate; the '*_assuming_neo_cache_hit_ratio' figures apply Gemini neo's observed 62% cache-read share for a like-for-like comparison. Gemini 'provider_reported' is the cost litellm recorded in the original runs (matches the flash PRICES formula).

gpu_cost.method: Each run records started_epoch/ended_epoch around run_one. usd_billed_wall_clock_union = 1.69 USD/h x union of the 15 run intervals (overlapping time counted once) = the GPU time these runs actually occupied. usd_if_runs_were_sequential = 1.69 x sum of per-run seconds (what it would cost one at a time, ignoring batching gains). Both exclude pod idle time, cold starts and the ~2 minutes of 3 runs that were killed mid-flight (see caveats); the pod bills flat per hour regardless, and part of the window was shared with another session's chat bench, so the marginal cost is at most these figures.

findings: Quality: qwen3-coder-next passed every task check (15/15) vs 13/20 for Gemini 2.5 Flash on identical settings and 17/20 for the best Gemini variant. Its biggest wins are T2 (answer-only question, 3/3 vs 0/4 neo) and T5 (feature + test, 3/3 vs 1/4 neo).

Harness false positive: T2 rep2 passed the check while stating shippingCents is correct (the check only looks for both function names in the answer). Strictly judged qwen is 14/15 (T2 2/3). The two Gemini T2 passes (today rep1, lean rep3) were audited and do name shippingCents as buggy.

Token volume: qwen uses ~1.5x the tokens of Gemini neo per run (mean 180k vs 121k) and ~1.5x the model calls (11.5 vs 7.6). The gap is in the automation tasks: T3 (192k vs 87k median, 11 vs 5.5 calls) and T4 (338k vs 118k, 18 vs 7 calls); qwen re-runs tests, adds reproduction commands and reviews pre-existing bugs. On T5 it is cheaper than Gemini (121k vs 234k) because Gemini neo flailed.
Fixed prefix: first-call prompt is ~12.0k tokens on chat tasks and ~14.4k on automation tasks, essentially the same as Gemini neo (tokenizer differences only).

Tool-name hallucinations: the logs (including the 3 interrupted runs) show 12 calls to tools that do not exist (read x6, run x3, read_file x2, write x1); the SDK returns an error and the model corrects itself on the next call, costing an extra round-trip each. No runs errored and none hit the 60-iteration cap. No sub-agent (task tool) use was observed in this bench.

Final messages: 8/15 runs ended without a final agent MessageEvent (finished via the finish tool), so final_message is empty; this does not affect any check except T2, where all three runs did produce a message.
Speed: mean 46 s per run vs 33 s for Gemini neo, while sharing the GPU with up to 5 other agent loops; T4 rep0 was the slowest at 141 s (25 calls).

Cost: at frontier (gemini-4-argon) prices qwen's token volume would cost $5.70 for the 15 runs ($0.38/run; $2.53 total / $0.17 per run with Gemini-like caching), versus $0.20-$0.33 of GPU time ($0.013-$0.022/run). Gemini Flash itself charged $0.021/run for neo; Gemini's own neo runs at argon prices would be $0.12/run. So self-hosting is ~same per-run cost as Gemini Flash and roughly 10-28x cheaper than the frontier model at this load, but only while the GPU is kept busy: an idle hour still costs $1.69.
caveats: 3 reps per task for qwen vs 4 for Gemini; small samples.
Settings are the round-3 'neo' variant, not the very latest app dump (which adds the newer AGENT_WORKING_RULES text).
Parallel runs (3 processes, plus another session's chat bench for the first minutes) make seconds an upper bound on single-run latency.

Three in-flight runs (T3 rep0, T5 rep1, T4 rep2) were killed at ~13:40 by an external process kill that also took down another session's qwen chat-bench runners; they were not recorded and were re-run from scratch (the resume logic skips only completed (task, rep) pairs). No pod restarts occurred, so every recorded run has attempts=1.
Gemini rows are from earlier the same day; provider load/time-of-day differ.
